transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (MonetaBank Head of AI), Sara Park (Infra Lead), Jamal Thompson (Security), Nina Alvarez (Product)

Summary (auto): MonetaBank evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production LLM inference. Primary ask is reserved capacity for latency-sensitive customer-facing workflows plus the ability to burst to hosted capacity for unpredictable peaks. Security and compliance requirements likely push them toward dedicated or private for PII workloads.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex AE on Redwood, and we'll run through how our Dedicated offering works and scope what MonetaBank needs. can you, carlos, give a quick overview of the workload?
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: yeah sure. so we have two main products: a customer support assistant and a fraud-scoring enrichment service. support assistant is the heavier one, about 100-150 requests per second at peak in certain regions, typical sequence length around 800-1,200 tokens, some longer threads. fraud enrichment is lower qps but needs <150 ms p50. we're evaluating whether to go hosted vs reserved dedicated. data residency and isolation are big ask for the bank.
[00:40] Priya Singh: ok, thanks. when you say 100-150 RPS is that concurrent requests or queries-per-second for generation calls? and are you using streaming?
[00:52] Carlos Mendez: mostly non-streaming for support (we return full response), but we can do streaming for some flows. so qps is generation calls, roughly 120 at peak across regions, may be spiky during mornings.
[01:10] Sara Park: one more infra detail - we prefer dedicated GPU pools for predictable latency; we are also curious about burst to hosted for spikes, so we don't overprovision. what does that look like?
[01:25] Alex Chen: good question. our Dedicated product gives you reserved capacity - a GPU pool you own logically. you pick the instance types (we recommend H100 or A100 depending on model), and you can configure burst policies to allow overflow to Redwood hosted. priya, do you want to add details on autoscale and bursting?
[01:40] Priya Singh: yeah. so, the baseline is reserved pools which are never preempted. for burst we can either use preconfigured burst capacity in your commitment (burst credits) or spill to hosted endpoints that we maintain. there's a tradeoff: bursting to hosted reduces cost of idle reserved resources but may increase tail latency if the hosted model has different SLOs. we also support a hybrid where critical routes pin to reserved nodes and others can overflow.
[02:05] Carlos Mendez: does bursting require network peering or is it transparent? we need to know about egress and data residency - we can't have certain PII go to hosted.
[02:16] Priya Singh: you can control routing policies per-route. we can mark PII-sensitive routes to never leave your dedicated pool; less-sensitive traffic can overflow. for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we can keep everything in your network, but that's a different engagement.
[02:32] Jamal Thompson: right, from security perspective we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention (minimum 12 months), and SAML SSO plus RBAC. also curious about key custody.
[02:43] Alex Chen: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM. audit logs and per-token traces are available in Redwood Console; retention and export can be part of the enterprise package.
[02:57] Speaker 1: (mumbled) can you also outline SLA for latency and uptime?
[03:03] Priya Singh: SLAs vary by plan; Dedicated gets the stronger SLOs. typical p50/p90 numbers we publish are for our verified model profiles but we also do customer-specific benchmarks. for reserved pools we offer an uptime SLA and a latency objective; we'll include the exact numbers in the follow-up.
[03:20] Nina Alvarez: operationally, how do updates and rollouts work? we can't have model changes suddenly degrade customer experience.
[03:28] Alex Chen: good - we do canary rollouts, A/Bs, and automatic fallback to previous model variants. Redwood Optimize can run prompt/eval monitoring so you get alerted for quality regressions.
[03:40] Carlos Mendez: ok, on sizing - how do you recommend we choose GPU counts? we were thinking maybe 8xA100 as starting point, can we model that?
[03:50] Priya Singh: yep. we typically estimate tokens/sec per GPU given model family, sequence length, and batching. for a 1,024-1,500 token avg and 120 qps, you may need something in the 6-12 GPU range depending on model and quantization. we will run a throughput est. for example, for a 30B opt-style model quantized to int8 you might get ~60-80 inference qps per A100 with small batch; H100 can be 1.5-2x depending on kernel.
[04:20] Carlos Mendez: and how does batching impact latency? we need sub-300ms p50 for most customer flows.
[04:27] Priya Singh: batching increases throughput but can add latency if you wait to accumulate tokens; Redwood's continuous batching minimizes wait by combining concurrent requests and KV cache reuse. you can set latency SLOs per route to limit batching window.
[04:45] Sara Park: regarding autoscaling - do you do per-GPU scaling or node level? can it be scheduled?
[04:53] Priya Singh: autoscaling is node-level for the pool; we support scheduled scaling and rules based on utilization or queue length. for bank workloads we recommend scheduled base capacity plus fast add policy for predictable daily spikes, and burst to hosted for rare flash events.
[05:10] Jamal Thompson: what about preemptible instances? we can't have preemptible for critical PII workflows.
[05:16] Alex Chen: preemptible/spot is only for non-critical, cost-optimization layers. reserved Dedicated pools are not preemptible.
[05:25] Carlos Mendez: curious about cost math - we don't want to pay for a lot of unused capacity for most times. how do teams typically structure this?
[05:32] Alex Chen: common pattern: commit to baseline reserved capacity to meet p95 latency for critical routes, then use burst credits or hosted overflow for peaks. Redwood Optimize helps identify which routes can be safely overflowed or quantized. we can show sample cost scenarios in the follow-up.
[05:52] Speaker 2: (background) are there limits on model variants per pool?
[05:56] Priya Singh: you can pin model versions and have multiple variants; one pool can host multiple models up to resource limits. mixing very different model sizes may reduce packing efficiency.
[06:08] Carlos Mendez: what network topologies do you support for Private? we have an on-prem cluster for regulated data.
[06:15] Alex Chen: Private supports VPC peering, private control plane, and an on-prem package. for on-prem we ship a deployable artifact and support offline air-gapped installs; full audit and KMS integration are part of that contract.
[06:30] Nina Alvarez: will we be able to run benchmarks ourselves? we'd like a perf run with our payloads.
[06:36] Priya Singh: yes, Priya will coordinate a benchmark. usually we ask for a representative prompt set + sequence length distribution, and we'll run throughput + p50/p90 latency in both dedicated and hosted fallback scenarios.
[06:48] Carlos Mendez: timeline wise, we want a pilot in the next 4-6 weeks. is that feasible?
[06:54] Alex Chen: yes, a 30-day pilot on dedicated is typical if procurement moves quickly. we'll need the pilots' expected traffic and the contract signature.
[07:05] (discussion continues with specifics)
[12:02] Priya Singh: (screen share note) I'm putting rough numbers: if your peak is 120 qps, average seq 1k tokens, and you want p50 <300ms, starting with 8xA100 with int8 quantization is a reasonable hypothesis; H100 reduces GPU count but may be pricier. we'll run a more precise GPU/sec tokens model and share a spreadsheet.
[12:27] Carlos Mendez: do you also support KV cache sharing across requests? some of our flows reuse context a lot which should lower cost.
[12:35] Priya Singh: yes, we support prefix/KV cache optimizations and session affinity when helpful. caching reduces repeated compute significantly for chatty sessions.
[12:47] Sara Park: since we have multiple regions, can we have dedicated pools per region and cross-region failover?
[12:54] Alex Chen: absolutely. you can provision regional pools, and our smart routing will direct traffic by latency policy and failover to other pools or hosted if the primary pool is constrained.
[13:10] Jamal Thompson: on audit logs retention - can we push logs to our SIEM?
[13:15] Alex Chen: yes, logs can be exported to your storage or forwarded to SIEMs; retention policy is configurable under enterprise package. we'll include the export endpoints in the security doc.
[13:28] Speaker 1: (unclear) any notes on model quantization support?
[13:32] Priya Singh: we support quantized deployments (int8, 4-bit depending on model) and can advise on quality/regression risk. Redwood Optimize includes quantization recommendations.
[13:45] Carlos Mendez: we also have a compliance review next week. Jamal will lead. we need Redwood's SOC2 and data flow diagram.
[13:53] Alex Chen: we'll send SOC2 and a network diagram. also the compliance pack link: https://redwood.example.com/enterprise-compliance (will attach in follow-up).
[14:08] Nina Alvarez: one corner case - if we want encryption-in-use (HSM-based) for model keys, is that supported?
[14:14] Priya Singh: yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and keys; for encryption-in-use there's options depending on environment - for private/on-prem you can keep key material on-prem. we'll confirm specifics in the security doc.
[14:30] (brief pause/background chatter)
[17:02] Priya Singh: quick technical note: when you overflow to hosted we keep request metadata minimal depending on policy; we don't persist payloads for overflowed non-PII routes. still, you should assume hosted endpoints are multi-tenant.
[17:20] Sara Park: what about regional data residency? we operate primarily in eu-west and us-east. can pools be restricted to regions?
[17:28] Alex Chen: yes, pools are regional. for Private you can deploy in specific regions or on-prem to satisfy residency.
[17:40] Carlos Mendez: what about burst cost delta vs reserved? rough numbers ok here.
[17:46] Alex Chen: bursting to hosted is billed at on-demand rates; reserved has a discount for committed capacity. we'll include a sample cost table in follow-up showing 50%, 80%, 100% utilization scenarios.
[18:05] (conversation about procurement timeline)
[21:00] Alex Chen: recap - Redwood to send pricing + SLA, Priya to run throughput estimates and propose GPU config and burst policy, Moneta to share traffic profile and compliance docs, schedule pilot start if procurement goes through.
[21:18] Carlos Mendez: thanks, that sounds good. any blockers from security? Jamal?
[21:24] Jamal Thompson: need SOC2, KMS details, network peering diagram, and confirmation of log retention/export. after that security sign-off should be straightforward.
[21:35] Alex Chen: we'll get those over. final Q - any immediate red flags?
[21:40] Nina Alvarez: nothing immediate, just want the benchmark and pricing to land this month.
[21:46] Alex Chen: great. we'll follow up with the items discussed and propose a pilot plan.

End of meeting.
